headline: US Restricts AI Compute Sales to China by Southeast Asian Data Hubs
summary: The US government introduced export licensing requirements for foreign data centres selling artificial intelligence computing power to Chinese entities, clouding tech investment across Southeast Asia.
why: Southeast Asian tech hubs like Malaysia and Singapore have become magnets for data centre expansion. Tighter US rules create regulatory hurdles for cross-border AI compute services.

impacts.name: Southeast Asian Data Centres
impacts.why: New US licensing rules limit customer bases and compute sales potential to Chinese clients.
